name: BetterHelp
one_liner: Online talk therapy with a licensed therapist by video, phone, live chat or messaging, paid by weekly subscription; some insurance plans now accepted.
best_for: Adults with mild to moderate depression, anxiety or stress who want weekly talk therapy from home
People who want to message a therapist between live sessions
People who can pay out of pocket or whose plan is accepted
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People who need medication or a psychiatric prescriber
People with severe mental illness who need intensive or in-person care
People who don't want their data handled by a company with a recent FTC privacy order
short_description: Subscription online therapy: you are matched with a licensed therapist for weekly live sessions plus messaging, about $70–$100 a week.
long_description: BetterHelp is a subscription online therapy service. After an intake questionnaire you are matched with a licensed therapist and can meet by video, phone or live chat, and message your therapist between sessions. BetterHelp's own pricing page puts the cost at about $70 to $100 a week, billed weekly or monthly; financial aid is available, and some insurance plans are now accepted, so check coverage at sign-up. It offers talk therapy only, not medication. In 2023 the FTC finalised an order that bans BetterHelp from sharing health data for advertising and required $7.8 million in refunds, after finding it had shared people's email addresses and health questionnaire answers with Facebook, Snapchat and others. The only published study of the service is a 2019 uncontrolled study of 318 users, in which depression scores fell over three months.
patient_summary: You fill in a questionnaire, get matched with a licensed therapist, and meet by video, phone or live chat, with messaging in between. You pay a subscription of about $70–$100 a week, billed weekly or every four weeks; financial aid is available and some insurance plans are accepted. Therapists do not prescribe medication.

pricing.notes: Price depends on location, preferences and therapist availability. Financial aid available for those who qualify. Some commercial insurance plans are accepted; check coverage during sign-up.

basis.regulatory_action: FTC order, 2023: shared email addresses and health questionnaire answers with Facebook, Snapchat and others for advertising; $7.8 million in refunds and a ban on sharing health data for ads

privacy.notes: Therapy records fall under the provider groups' HIPAA notice, but website visitor data can be shared for advertising if you accept ad cookies, and a 2023 FTC order covers past ad sharing of health data.

seo.title: BetterHelp: Online Therapy Platform Review | HeyPsych
seo.meta_description: BetterHelp is the largest online therapy platform connecting users with licensed therapists via text, phone, or video for $65-100/week, not covered by insura...

faqs.a: BetterHelp costs $65-100 per week, billed monthly ($260-400/month). This includes unlimited messaging with your therapist plus one live session per week. Financial aid is available for qualifying individuals. BetterHelp does NOT accept insurance, so this is entirely out-of-pocket.

No, BetterHelp is not covered by insurance or health plans. It's an out-of-pocket expense. If you need insurance-covered therapy, consider platforms like Teladoc, Amwell, Cerebral, or Talkspace (which offers insurance options), or use your insurance's mental health directory.

Yes, BetterHelp connects you with licensed therapists (psychologists, LCSWs, LPCs, LMFTs). However, the convenience trade-off means you may not get the depth of in-person care. It works well for general mental wellness but isn't appropriate for severe conditions, trauma requiring specialized treatment, or crisis situations.

faqs.q: How is BetterHelp different from Talkspace?
faqs.a: Both are large online therapy platforms. BetterHelp is slightly cheaper and has more therapists but doesn't accept insurance. Talkspace accepts some insurance plans and offers psychiatry services. Both offer text messaging plus live sessions. Choose based on whether you have insurance coverage and need medication management.
